messages:
Ethan Wu: Hi all, new hire here. Trying to get kubectl working for `redwood-staging` but my context keeps falling back to `default` and `kubectl describe pod` gives 403. I think my kubeconfig got merged from multiple guides. macOS Ventura, iTerm2, zsh. Any tips?

Lena Gomez: Welcome Ethan! :wave: Can you paste the output of `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config view --flatten --minify`? Also, are you using AWS SSO or a static token?

Ethan Wu: Current context: `arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:999999999999:cluster/redwood-staging`
`kubectl config view --minify --flatten` shows an `exec` user that calls `aws sts get-caller-identity` via the `aws` plugin. I also have an old `~/.kube/config.backup` that I merged manually.

Jordan Lee: Two things we've seen: 1) merged kubeconfigs can keep old `users`/`contexts` entries with the same cluster name which confuses `kubectl`, and 2) if you have multiple `KUBECONFIG` files set, the precedence order can cause unexpected contexts. Run `echo $KUBECONFIG` and `kubectl config view --raw` to inspect.

Ethan Wu: KUBECONFIG is unset. I only have `~/.kube/config` but I manually copied lots of entries into it.

Lena Gomez: Ok. Easiest fix: create a fresh minimal kubeconfig that contains only the staging cluster + an alias context that pins your namespace. Save a backup first: `cp ~/.kube/config ~/.kube/config.pre-ethan`. Then run:
```
kubectl config view --raw > ~/.kube/config.full
kubectl config set-context ethan-staging --cluster=redwood-staging --user=arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:999999999999:exec --namespace=redwood-staging
kubectl config use-context ethan-staging
```
That `--user` value is just an alias; the real exec plugin will populate creds when you `aws sso login`.

Jordan Lee: Also, confirm you have RBAC for namespace `redwood-staging`. If `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n redwood-staging` returns `no`, we can create a `RoleBinding` to give your GH user `ethanw` `view` rights for the namespace. Which GitHub handle should we use?

Ethan Wu: My GH handle is `ethanw`. I ran `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n redwood-staging` and got `no`.

Lena Gomez: I'll create a RoleBinding for you scoped to that namespace and also add a short script to generate a clean kubeconfig for new hires. Give me a minute.

ops-bot: [system] rolebinding/redwood-staging-view created by Lena Gomez at 2026-03-24T09:12:40Z

Lena Gomez: RoleBinding created. Try `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n redwood-staging` again. Also if you want we can generate a serviceaccount token instead (namespace-scoped) for short-term access without SSO hassle.

Ethan Wu: `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n redwood-staging` now returns `yes`. I can `kubectl get pods -n redwood-staging` and `kubectl logs` too. Thanks!

Jordan Lee: If you still see context flips, consider using `kubectl config rename-context` to remove ambiguous names, e.g.: `kubectl config rename-context arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:999999999999:cluster/redwood-staging redwood-staging-ethan`. Also we added a short doc `docs/onboarding/kube-cleanup.md` showing the minimal kubeconfig flow for new hires.

Ethan Wu: Perfect. I'll update my checklist and the onboarding doc I maintain. Appreciate the quick help :tada:
